newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Navia eager for Whessoe.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Navia eager for Whessoe.

text.p: Norwegian navigation and communication equipment maker Seatex Garex ASA, soon to be renamed Navia, said on Wednesday it had made a joint bid for Britain's Whessoe Plc at a hefty premium to an earlier bid by Siebe Plc because it expected a better industrial fit.
"Our bid is 100 percent complementary, while Siebe would probably have to do some restucturing," Navia chief executive Hans Olav Torsen told Reuters in a London telehone interview.
"Even at this increased level our bid is very much earnings enhancing (for Navia)," Torsen added. Navia's partner is privately-owned Swiss process controls group Endress + Hauser.
Like Whessoe itself, Navia and E+H are both relatively small players in the specialist controls and instruments business.
In that respect they differ from Siebe which has a global presence in several major electronic controls markets and a market capitalisation of several billion pounds.

Siebe is a broadly diversified engineer, with over 150 companies across the world, and involved in the manufacture and design of components and systems in many areas beyond those in which Whessoe has a presence.
Torsen argued that Siebe would have areas of overlap with Whessoe units but the Swiss-Norwegian partners would not.
Navia has taken a two-thirds interest in the 10.6 percent of Whessoe shares it and E+H have already bought privately.

This ratio reflects the planned division of the assets of Whessoe which the partners have decided upon -- the biggest prize being Autronica, Whessoe's Norway-based marine instruments and security unit, which would be combined with Navia.
"Autronica fits perfectly with our main operations in Norway as well as expanding our marine and offshore technology business worldwide," Torsen said in the launch statement.
His Swiss counterpart Klaus Riemenschneider said the Whessoe units E+H was keen to acquire would be a platform for new growth.
For E+H, Torsen stressed, Whessoe offered an opportunity for the Swiss company to expand in the U.S market, especially in the tank and liquid level measurement sector.
According to Torsen, the impact on Navia's financial position of a completed deal would be to effectively double its turnover to about 1.0 billion crowns per year.
At the current price, he said the cash and debt-funded offer would lead to a fall in Navia's equity ratio to between 25 and 30 percent from its current 60 percent level.
"We can still live with that... I think Autronica is a fairly mature business," he added.
By Wednesday afternoon Siebe had made no statement on the likely impact on its agreed 46 million stg offer of the European companies' 52.6 million stg bid.
Torsen declined to comment on how his partnership would react to any increase in the Siebe price, saying only: "time will tell".
